title: Up More Than 12% This Year, Is This Dividend Stock With an Ultra-High Yield a No-Brainer Buy? - The Motley Fool
summary: Up More Than 12% This Year, Is This Dividend Stock With an Ultra-High Yield a No-Brainer Buy? The Motley Fool
body:
While major indexes and many growth stocks started 2026 sluggishly, investors have been finding their way back to value and dividend stocks. One beneficiary has been Altria (MO 0.77%), which is up more than 12% year to date as of March 26.

It's obviously a plus that Altria's stock is up, but its main selling point to investors is its consistently attractive dividend. It's routinely one of the highest you'll find in the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.72%).

Given its nice start to the year and lucrative dividend, is Altria a no-brainer buy? Well, it depends on the investor.

body:
Altria Group Inc. (MO) has historically delivered strong annual returns, driven by consistent dividend growth and the tobacco industry's resilience. According to a recent report from Yahoo Finance, the stock's performance has been more modest over the past ten years as U.S. smoking rates fall and diversification attempts have largely been unsuccessful.

Notable setbacks include investments in Cronos Group and Juul Labs that resulted in significant financial losses. A more recent acquisition, NJOY, encountered a regulatory obstacle when a federal commission banned the sale of certain NJOY products due to patent infringement.

Despite these issues, Altria's share price has increased approximately 50% in the last two years, aligning with a sector-wide rise fueled by optimism around smoke-free alternatives. The company's On! oral nicotine pouches represent one such product.

Nevertheless, Altria's fundamental cigarette business is contracting. The primary risk for the company is a potential failure to transition successfully to next-generation, non-combustible products.

Recent financial data shows a pattern of declining revenue, offset by profit growth achieved through price increases. For the 2025 fiscal year, revenue after excise taxes decreased slightly, while adjusted earnings per share saw a modest rise.

The volume of domestic cigarette shipments fell sharply. The strategy of raising prices on a product with rapidly declining consumption is viewed as unsustainable. Shipments for the On! brand increased for the full year, though growth nearly stalled in the final quarter amid competitive promotional activity from a rival product.

For 2026, Altria is forecasting earnings-per-share growth within a specific range. This projected growth, combined with the stock's dividend yield, represents a solid potential return.

Altria's decade-long push to diversify beyond cigarettes has yet to produce substantial results. This stands in contrast to some industry competitors, which are reportedly achieving greater traction with their own smoke-free portfolios.
